L12·N8485unmasked layer
Largely a suppression-direction neuron: its few positive hits are function-word tokens inside conditional/definitional clauses ("falls **on a** Saturday", "if the format **is** supported", "%," in a rate calculation), while it is strongly negatively driven by clause-embedding perception/report verbs and their complementizers ("we've heard **that**", "people **find**", "tests **revealed**", "felt too **warm**").

L31·N7569unmasked layer
Fires on the delimiter token that introduces a spelled-out name/acronym gloss — typically the opening parenthesis right after an organization/term name (BODHI (…, Best Efficiency Point (BEP), BAAPS)), and similar boundary marks (opening quote before "robots", a URL slash-segment, a paragraph newline); notably the same parenthesis context can also strongly *suppress* it (e.g. "(MUFAs"), so it is a punctuation/boundary detector rather than a clean acronym feature.
